name: inprocess-obi-apb-three-ip-timer-multilink-i2c-spi-f5
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches three APB3 targets in one process, and the first target declares two real IRQ links: the PULP timer's overflow (irq_o[0]) and compare (irq_o[1]) outputs. The PULP I2C and PULP SPI each declare one link, so the session's global table has four links over three targets. One F5 case selects one global link; its trigger writes, ISR status read and clear write all belong to that link's own target and status word. The two-source row is absent by name (unsupported-f5:both-needs-one-link-per-target): the pair's per-target counters cannot tell the timer's two links apart, and the ISR carries two cell sets.
notes: Three APB3 target rows, one generated model each. Windows: timer 0x40001000..0x40001fff, I2C 0x40002000..0x40002fff, SPI 0x20002000..0x20002fff; all are the profiles' own 4 KiB windows and pairwise disjoint, and disjoint from the RAM image 0x10000..0x30000.

Target 0's behavior is configs/behaviors/pulp_timer_multilink_f5.json: a v2 irq_sources list with two links on the same physical port irq_o - bit 0 (overflow, status TIMER0_COUNT at offset 0, triggers [[4,0],[8,0],[0,0xffffffff]]) and bit 1 (compare, status TIMER0_CMP at offset 8, triggers [[4,0],[8,3],[0,3]]). Both are pulse outputs with no clear. Target 1 is the PULP I2C (configs/peripherals/pulp_i2c_irq, configs/behaviors/pulp_i2c_level_f5.json): level interrupt_o, STATUS at 0xc, clear CMD=1. Target 2 is the PULP SPI (configs/peripherals/inprocess_verify_pulp_spi_irq, configs/behaviors/pulp_spi_eot_f5.json): pulse events_o[1], INTSTA at 0x28, no clear.

All four links declare three trigger writes, so one F5 record shape (global link index plus three trigger values) serves every row. The global table is 0 = timer overflow, 1 = timer compare, 2 = I2C level, 3 = SPI end-of-transfer.

The synthetic two-source row is refused by name: unsupported-f5:both-needs-one-link-per-target. The timer owns two links, and the pair's per-target read/clear counters and the two ISR cell sets cannot attribute two simultaneously asserted links of one target. This session therefore proves per-link selection over a four-row table, not simultaneous attribution; the three-target single-link scenario is where the both row runs.
The I2C pad inputs and the SPI serial inputs are held at their idle values in fixed_inputs and tuning.fixed_inputs, and no 32-bit pad group is selected.
No dma_profile is declared, so F6 is refused by name (unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:apb3).
This file declares the scenario; it is not evidence. The real RTL run under runs/p1-irq/ is the evidence.
